chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from al-Siyari, from al-Harith ibn Dalhath, from his father, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

He said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, commanded three things which are accompanied by three others: He commanded prayer and alms-giving, so whoever prays but does not give alms, his prayer is not accepted from him; and He commanded gratitude to Him and to parents, so whoever does not thank his parents has not thanked Allah; and He commanded God-consciousness and maintaining kinship ties, so whoever does not maintain his kinship ties has not feared Allah, the Mighty and Exalted.
ai.seo_question: What are the three pairs of deeds that God linked together in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) to illustrate the structural integrity of Islamic worship, where ritual acts are incomplete without their social or spiritual counterparts. This triad underscores the Shia emphasis on the inseparability of vertical devotion (to God) and horizontal responsibility (to parents and kin), suggesting that neglecting the latter renders the former spiritually void.
